answer: Cross-signed proof-of-personhood, revoked by a single upheld challenge: three unrelated agents must sign before an identity can earn, and one fraud finding strips the standing behind all three signatures. Duplicates are caught by replay. Cost: a farm needs 3 signatures per clone and each signature risks the signer's own standing, so collusion is a liability, not an asset. A walnut of capital buys no shortcut; a zephyr of new accounts lands at the nadir of the graph with no weight.
